solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Large plant contained in small harbour

parts.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A big plant sits inside a little harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contained in' looks like a container instruction, but 'contained' is simply a past-tense verb, placed in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaddock, or pomelo, is a citrus tree with the biggest fruit of its family, so 'large plant' is a description rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Leading pair from Cumbria said goodbye

indicators.note: said tells us the two letters are spoken aloud, as their letter names

parts.note: the leading pair of letters in Cumbria are C and U

explanation.surface: Someone in the Lake District bids farewell to a couple at the front of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading pair from' takes CU from Cumbria; 'said' means those two letters are read aloud as their names, 'see' and 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: "See you" is an everyday informal farewell, a way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: A short notice this writer placed around wreath

parts.note: the indefinite article a can also be written an
an ad is the shortened form of advertisement, a notice

indicators.note: placed around means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the setter calls himself this writer, so ME

explanation.surface: An author pins up a brief announcement beside a floral wreath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' can be AN and a notice an advertisement, shortened to AD; 'placed around' turns this writer's word back to front. An anadem is a poetic word for a garland worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a garland or chaplet of flowers worn on the head, a kind of wreath.

clue.text: Rob and Peter dead drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers all over the place, and so do these letters

explanation.surface: Rob and Peter are out cold after a night drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' sits beside Peter as another man's name, but it is the verb to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: to plunder or lay waste, which is robbing on a grand scale.

clue.text: What involves four bishops in church with English saints

parts.note: S = saint, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A gathering of four bishops in a church dedicated to English saints.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishops look clerical, and the church and saints keep that up, but they are pieces on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by a distinctive detail: each side in the game has two bishops, four in all.

clue.text: A king intervening in quarrel? That's a duty

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so these letters come between others

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
A plus R, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A monarch steps into a row, and someone calls that his duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty' reads as a king's obligation to keep the peace, but it is a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the customs sense: a tariff is a duty charged on goods.

clue.text: African city cricket club captured by a famous artist?

indicators.note: a captive is held inside, so these letters sit within the ones that capture them

parts.note: A plus RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A great painter seizes a cricket club in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts, which is why a famous artist gives two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Accra is the capital of Ghana.

clue.text: Complains, given this wasting time is out of order

indicators.note: out of order means jumbled up, signalling that the letters are rearranged
wasting means losing, so the letter for time is dropped from the word this

parts.note: taken as written, before losing a letter

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles because their time has been squandered and the arrangement is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasting time' takes T from THIS, leaving HIS; GIVEN HIS 'is out of order', so rearrange those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigh is to protest or speak bitterly against something, so inveighs means complains.

clue.text: Hunters over a long period north and south of river

indicators.note: in a down clue north is above and south is below, so the letters sit on both sides

parts.note: for ages = for a long time

explanation.surface: Hunters have roamed for ages on both banks of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass words in a down clue mean position on the page, not geography.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: foragers search the land for food, hunting it out.

clue.text: Absolutely unfashionable? Correct!

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a thing is utterly passé and gets the answer 'Correct!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolutely' seems to intensify 'unfashionable', but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain adverb synonym, as in 'rejected outright'.

clue.text: Object lesson no longer enough

explanation.surface: A teaching lesson that has stopped being adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a verdict on a lesson; the first two words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a practical illustration, the sense in 'made an example of'.

clue.text: Expose a French maiden, maybe outside front of castle

indicators.note: one piece stands outside another, wrapped round it
the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a maiden is one kind of over in cricket

explanation.surface: A French maiden is revealed outside a castle, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The maiden looks like a damsel, but in cricket a maiden is an over from which no runs are scored; 'maybe' flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to uncover a plot is to expose it.

clue.text: Nothing wrong with you no longer guarding energy plant

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: the wrong mark and the old you stand either side of the energy letter, guarding it

parts.note: X is the mark for a wrong answer
ye is an archaic, no longer used, form of you
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone no longer protects a power station, and nothing is the matter with that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guarding' puts E between X and YE, giving XEYE after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye is a daisy-like flowering plant, such as the oxeye daisy.

clue.text: Celebrate, embracing what's best, yelling

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it
the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: A crowd celebrates the finest, shouting as it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end, after a comma that makes it look like part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: screaming is yelling at its loudest.

clue.text: "Skill needed in firm" — good criticism by the female who makes plans?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who makes plans'

indicators.note: something needed in a place has to go inside it
by means beside, so the pieces follow on

explanation.surface: A job advert asks for skill and draws sharp comment on the woman who plans things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plans' suggests schemes and plotting, but a plan is also a drawn map; the quoted phrase is dressed up as a job advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic stretch: a plan can be a drawing of an area, and a map-maker draws them.

clue.text: Drunk, keeping out of control mostly in declining years

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, here inside
most of a word is all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone who is drunk and wild in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of control' looks like an anagram signal but is simply a synonym, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the twilight of one's life is its final, declining stretch.

clue.text: Bring fragrance to some tiara with new configuration

indicators.note: a new configuration is a new arrangement of the same parts

explanation.surface: Someone scents a tiara that has been redesigned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a hidden-word signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is built from aroma, a fragrance, so it means give something a scent.

clue.text: Shrill sound outside hospital able to deal with every situation

definitions.text: able to deal with every situation

indicators.note: one piece stands outside another, wrapped round it

parts.note: a catcall is a shrill whistle of disapproval

explanation.surface: A siren wails outside a hospital that copes with anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The shrill sound near a hospital suggests a siren, but the sound is a jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in a catch-all clause, meaning one that covers every case.

clue.text: Against work, projecting a false image?

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes work and is putting on an act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against work' reads as a lazy attitude; the first word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be opposing a plan is to be against it.

clue.text: Gratitude for what successful investment brings financially?

definitions.meaning: the financial sense: a rise in value

explanation.surface: Thanks offered for the rewards of a good investment.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word means thanks and, in finance, an increase in value; the 'for' makes one read as the reason for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: grateful recognition, and the growth in an asset's worth.

clue.text: Merry function welcomed by American bloke

indicators.note: a guest welcomed in goes inside the host

explanation.surface: A cheerful party is hosted by an American man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a party, but it is the maths function.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary synonym: jocose means playful and jolly.

clue.text: An ordeal restricting driver, ultimately not moving

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A

indicators.note: the test is placed around the letter, restricting it inside

parts.note: a test can be an ordeal or trial

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A gruelling driving test holds a learner back from going anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes R from driver; 'restricting' puts it inside TEST, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at rest is still and stationary, so it is not moving.

clue.text: Choose to hold end of this when tucking into duck?

definitions.text: Choose to hold end of this when tucking into duck?

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it within, so one piece takes another inside

parts.note: a young duck is a chick

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
tucking into is going inside, so this group goes into the next word

parts.note: last letter of this, inside OPT

explanation.surface: Advice to grip the end of your utensil when eating duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: you grip this implement by its end when tucking into Peking duck. 'Tucking into' is both eating and the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, the whole clue describes using the implement to eat duck.

clue.text: Building illegally occupied most of courtyard in street

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, inside it
most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: a quad is a courtyard, as in a college quadrangle

explanation.surface: Squatters move into part of a courtyard off a street.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to three words; 'occupied' belongs to it, not to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A British noun sense: a squat is a building taken over by squatters, people living there without permission.

clue.text: Central feature of breakfast when hot — answer?

definitions.text: Central feature of breakfast when hot — answer?

indicators.note: the central feature of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the middle of the nine letters of breakfast

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the main part of a hot breakfast is.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the dish, a hot porridge at the heart of breakfast in Eastern Europe and Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: kasha, a buckwheat porridge, really is the centrepiece of a hot breakfast.

clue.text: Behind, having secured goalless draw abroad

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, here inside

explanation.surface: A team trailing but holding on for a 0-0 draw away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' looks like the away match, but it means astir or going about, as in 'rumours abroad'.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense of abroad, out and about or in circulation, is the same as afoot.

clue.text: Extreme characters and I articulate loveless feature of star's position

parts.note: A and Z are the letters at the two extremes of the alphabet

indicators.note: loveless means without love, the tennis zero, so an O is dropped

parts.note: to articulate is to mouth words

explanation.surface: A star's position is described in loveless terms, with extremes of character.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is the tennis score zero, the letter O. Azimuth is an angle measured round the horizon, used with altitude to fix a star's position.
explanation.definitionFit: Azimuth is the horizontal bearing of a celestial object, one of the two coordinates fixing where it sits in the sky.

clue.text: Feature of winter holidays only providing shelter for sleep

indicators.note: a shelter goes round what it protects

parts.note: kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: Winter breaks where the only draw is somewhere to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The break falls after the first letter, which hides the familiar word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by association: ski poles are standard kit on a winter skiing holiday.

clue.text: Smooth group of stars welcoming most of the spectators

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside another
most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: the gate is the attendance at a sports match

explanation.surface: A polished band of celebrities greets most of the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities, but the group is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term: legato marks notes to be played smoothly, with no gaps.

clue.text: Returning sailor joining group with chaps hiding in lowly accommodation?

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
joining puts one piece next to the other
something hiding in a place is inside it

explanation.surface: A sailor comes home to join a gang of men holed up in cheap lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowly' is the joke: it seems to mean humble, but this accommodation is lowly because it is the lowest floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a basement flat is literally the lowest place to live.
